newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Serbs block refugee voter route - OSCE.
newsitem.headline: Serbs block refugee voter route - OSCE.

text.p: Bosnian Serb authorities have blocked one of 19 special routes set up to allow Moslem and Croat refugees to vote in their former home area on Saturday, international organisers of Bosnia's elections said.

Jeff Fischer, director general of elections for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), told reporters in Sarajevo that Serb police had refused to open the route to the Prijedor area in northwest Bosnia.
"The voter route to the Prijedor (polling area) has been blocked," he said. "The chief of police (in the district) has said he does not want the route to Prijedor to be open."

Fischer said troops of the NATO-led peace Implementation Force (IFOR), which has secured all 19 routes across Bosnia's internal ethnic boundaries, were "negotiating to make him abide by the agreements signed by (local police) ministers".

Elsewhere, he said, Serbs had stopped seven buses taking Moslem refugees from Kladanj to Vlasenica in Serb-held eastern Bosnia. "IFOR and (U.N. police monitors) are taking action and we expect this problem to be solved soon," he told Bosnian state television.
